info.title: Trema API
info.description:
The public REST API for Trema, the AI agent your company owns.

## Authentication

The API accepts two kinds of credentials:

- **Session cookie** — for browsers and interactive clients. Sign in through the auth endpoints under `/api/auth/*` to receive the session cookie. Organization-scoped operations act as the signed-in member of the active organization.
- **Service credential** — for machines. An administrator creates one with `POST /service-credentials` and receives the secret once. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer trema_sc_...`. The token acts as the principal it is bound to.

Each operation lists the scheme it accepts. Operations that list no scheme are public.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie set by sign-in. Over HTTPS the cookie name carries the `__Secure-` prefix.

serviceCredential.description: An organization-scoped service credential. The secret is shown once at creation and acts as the principal the credential is bound to.

sessionToken.description: A context session token. Opening a session returns it once; it expires after fifteen minutes and renewal extends it.

get.description: Report which model the stored vectors were produced by, and how many items still need one. The embedding model is part of the index, so a vector written by a model the `embed` role no longer names is ignored by search until a reindex replaces it. Nothing here reaches a provider.

post.description: Resolve a surface location to a scope and open a session against it. The response carries the session token, the standing context, and the pinned policy snapshot.

dm.description: Whether the location is a one-to-one conversation with the agent. A linked person's DM resolves to their personal scope.

threadRef.description: The thread this session belongs to, when the surface has threads.

externalUserId.description: The requesting person's raw surface id.

principalId.description: The requesting person's principal ID. A UUID.

requester.description: Who asked. Omit it for scheduled work that nobody triggered.

schema.description: The location and requester to open a session for.

sessionId.description: The session's unique ID. A UUID (version 7).

sessionToken.description: The bearer token for this session's data-plane calls. Returned only once.

expiresAt.description: When the session token expires. An ISO 8601 date-time. Renewal extends it.

mode.description: The session's identity mode. `service` acts as the organization's agent; `delegated` acts as the requesting person.

id.description: The scope's unique ID. A UUID (version 7).

name.description: The scope's display name.

items.description: One scope in the session's resolution chain.

scopeChain.description: The scopes the session reads, widest first. Writes land at the last one.

instructions.description: The scope chain's active instructions, concatenated widest to narrowest.

type.description: The memory type, such as `rule` or `preference`.

rules.description: The standing memories that fit the token budget, most-recently-reinforced first.

skillIndex.description: A name and description line per installed skill.

budgetTokens.description: The token budget the standing set was cut at.

usedTokens.description: The estimated token cost of the injected content.

overflowItemIds.description: Standing items the budget cut. They remain reachable through search.

standing.description: The bounded set of context injected into every turn of this session.

tools.description: The tool definitions this session may call.

post.description: Report the messages of the thread this session serves — the people's and the agent's. The thread is identified by the session's surface location, so repeated sessions on it extend one conversation. Reporting the same batch twice changes nothing.

schema.description: The ID of the session reporting the messages. A UUID.

surfaceMessageRef.description: The surface's own id for the message. It is the dedup key: reporting it again edits the stored message instead of adding a second one.

operation.description: `upsert` lands a new message or edits the one with this reference; `delete` removes it, for a message retracted on the surface. Defaults to `upsert`.

principalId.description: The author's principal ID. A UUID.

externalRef.description: The author's raw surface id. An id that is linked to a person also records the principal.

author.description: Who said it. Required for `upsert`, ignored for `delete`.

sentAt.description: When the message was sent. Required for `upsert`, ignored for `delete`.

text.description: What was said. Required for `upsert`, ignored for `delete`.

items.description: One reported message.

messages.description: The messages to report, oldest first.

schema.description: A batch of messages to capture on the session's thread.

conversationId.description: The conversation the messages landed on.

scopeId.description: The scope the conversation belongs to.

threadRef.description: The thread within the location. Empty when the surface reported none.

updated.description: How many stored messages the batch edited.

unchanged.description: How many messages were already stored as reported.

deleted.description: How many stored messages the batch removed.

notFound.description: How many deletions named a message that was not stored.

messageCount.description: How many messages the conversation holds after the batch.

lastActivityAt.description: The conversation's latest activity. An ISO 8601 date-time.

seq.description: The message's place in the thread. Null when there was nothing to act on.

results.description: One result per reported message, in the order reported.

schema.description: What the batch did to the conversation.
